Claim: PM loop round 7 — `domain:cli` seat.

- Session: `session_01B3Kurx8qufrDzNjk4rag7V` (account `hotlong`)
- Branch: `claude/issue-7749-meta-put-actor-identity`
- Worktree: dedicated (cloud container)
- Domain: `domain:cli`
- File surface: `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts` — the `/meta` PUT/publish/rollback handler region and the five actor-resolution sites (~:5846, :5965, :6110, :6164, :6516 on `origin/main`, line numbers will have drifted) + tests. Stop on breach; explain in the report.
- Container & model: M, `mode:cloud`, `model: claude-opus-5`.
- Serial constraints cleared: the only in-flight cli claim is #7602 (`packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts`). `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts` is otherwise free — #7930 (`mapDataError`) and #7907 (`_drafts`) both merged. ⚠️ Two queued cards also land in this file (#7678 suggested-bindings, and #7748's family) — they are NOT dispatched and will be serialized behind this one by region.

### 裁决:修生产者,⛔ 不要再加一条 fallback

`req.user` / `req.userId` are unset on this path and the header is the only limb that ever resolves. The fix is to make the authenticated identity **actually reach these handlers**, not to widen the fallback chain — adding another `??` limb would leave the same "declared identity that nobody produces" shape the card is reporting, one level down. This is a no-producer defect: the bearer token *is* validated, its identity just never lands on the request the handler reads.

Fix it at the one place that serves all five sites if the code allows; if the sites genuinely need separate treatment, say why in the report rather than copy-pasting a fix five times — one rule in five copies is what this lane has spent the shift undoing.

### ⚠️ Report on this, do NOT change it unilaterally

Read the chain as written:

```
req.headers['x-actor'] ?? req.user?.id ?? req.userId
```

**The header wins over the authenticated identity.** Once `req.user` is populated, that ordering means an authenticated caller can still attribute a metadata write to somebody else by sending `X-Actor` — the audit trail would name whoever the header says. Today that is masked because the other two limbs are always `undefined`; fixing the producer makes the precedence live and load-bearing for the first time.

⛔ Do **not** silently reorder or drop the header limb as part of this card. Some service-to-service or impersonation flow may legitimately depend on it, and changing whose name lands in an audit row is a security-semantics decision, not a bug fix. **Measure and report**: who sets `X-Actor` in this repo and in the console, whether any caller depends on it out-ranking the session, and what the audit contract says it means. If it turns out nothing legitimate sets it, say so — that makes it a clean follow-up card rather than a guess. I will take the ordering question to the maintainer with your measurement.

### Pin the consequence
- An admin **bearer**-authenticated `PUT /api/v1/meta/<type>/<name>` with **no** `X-Actor` records that admin's id — in the **audit** row (not `'system'`) **and** the **history** row (not `null`). Both, since they default differently and a fix that only satisfies one is half-done.
- Negative: a genuinely unauthenticated / internal system write still records `system` — ⛔ the fix must not start stamping a real user onto machine writes.
- Regression: an explicit `X-Actor` still behaves exactly as it does today (whatever the reported ordering turns out to be) — so this PR is separable from the precedence decision.

**Premise-first**: the filer verified the five sites on `00e9196`; re-verify on current `origin/main` and find them by text, not line number (many PRs merged since). #7748 is a *different* defect (publish/rollback writes no audit row at all) — ⛔ do not fix it here, but note that once it lands its rows inherit this bug, so a shared fix location is worth naming if you see one.

## ACCEPTED — PR #7940. Landing on gate-green.

Reviewed by the `domain:cli` seat (`hotlong`, session `session_01B3Kurx8qufrDzNjk4rag7V`) against the diff.

### The producer was fixed once, and wired to the right identity

`resolveMetaWriteActor` replaces the two dead limbs at all five sites — save, delete, publish, rollback, compound save — rather than adding a third limb or being copy-pasted five times. And it resolves through `resolveExecCtx`, **the same identity resolution the route's own `manage_metadata` capability gate reads a few lines earlier**, with the consequence stated better than my dispatch put it:

> the caller a write is ATTRIBUTED to can never drift from the caller it was AUTHORIZED against.

That is the property worth having. `resolveExecCtx` is memoized per request, so the routes that already resolved a context for their gate pay nothing extra.

### The test boots the real stack, for a stated reason

The two defaults that swallowed the identity live **downstream of REST and differ** — `sys_metadata_audit.actor` falls back to the string `'system'`, `sys_metadata_history.recorded_by` to SQL `NULL`. So a mock asserting "REST passed an `actor` field" would have proven neither row, and a fix satisfying only one would have passed. Instead: a real better-sqlite3 `:memory:` engine, the real `sys_metadata*` object definitions, a real protocol, the real route — and the assertions read the **persisted rows**.

Both rows are asserted **together in one object** (`{audit, history}` → `{ADMIN, ADMIN}`), explicitly so that a half-fix cannot pass on the strength of the first assertion. That is a small thing that matters: two sequential `expect`s would have let a `'system'`-in-history regression hide behind a green audit assertion.

The last case is the one I would have accepted the PR without and been slightly poorer for: it **removes the `execCtx` stub entirely** and drives the production `bearer → getSession → resolveAuthzContext → execCtx` chain against a real auth service, then asserts `resolveMetaWriteActor` turns exactly that into the recorded actor. The other three cases stub the auth boundary; this one closes the loop and proves the link the card said was missing.

Negatives are pinned as required: an internal `isSystem` write still records `'system'` / `NULL` (⛔ the fix does not invent a user for machine writes), and an anonymous caller is refused **401** with **no row at all**.

### The modified existing assertion was changed for the right reason

`rest.test.ts` previously asserted `expect(arg).not.toHaveProperty('actor')`. That is now `expect(arg.actor).toBe('test-user')`, with the justification that **the absence was the defect, not the contract** — it encoded the very bug this card reports. Changing an existing expectation to accommodate your own diff is the move I check hardest, and this one explains why the old expectation was wrong rather than merely noting that it changed.

One edge handled and documented: a *present-but-unusable* header (repeated → array, or empty string) falls through to the session rather than suppressing attribution — recording the real caller beats recording `'system'` for a malformed request.

### ⚠️ The `X-Actor` precedence is correctly left alone, and is now mine to carry

`X-Actor` still outranks the authenticated identity, exactly as before — and the PR says plainly that this becomes load-bearing for the first time now that the other limb produces a value, i.e. an authenticated caller can attribute a metadata write to somebody else. Leaving it unchanged was the instruction and the right call: whose name lands in an audit row is a security-semantics decision for the audit contract, not a side effect of fixing a producer. The test that pins today's ordering is even labelled as *the test to change when the maintainer rules*.

**That question does not close with this PR.** I am filing it separately with the dev's measurement attached, so the ordering is decided deliberately rather than inherited by default — and so this fix is not read as an endorsement of it.

### Scope
4 files: `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`, a new row-level test, one existing-test update, changeset. No `docs/adr/**`, no skills paths, no `content/docs/releases/`.

⛔ Not flipped yet: ESLint and TypeScript Type Check must both read `conclusion: success`. ⚠️ The new test registers objects with an explicit `packageId` specifically to avoid adding to `packages/rest`'s frozen type-error pile — the right instinct, and the ratchet will confirm it.
